html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 9. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and the run results: the camera changes job to WATER and then JUICE, the stray bottle of the old product is rejected, the first trace record reads SODA,01,000001, the level completes, every bottle in the right bin, under par.

Level 8 had one product. This line runs three, one batch after another: eight SODA, eight WATER, eight JUICE. Each product has its own camera job, because each has its own bottle, label and fill line: SODA passes at 95 % of the label, WATER at 90 %, JUICE at 97 %. Between batches the program has to do what an operator does at a real changeover: hold the infeed, let the last bottle of the old product clear the camera, load the next job and wait for the camera to confirm it, then start feeding again.

Two more things come with it. Every changeover leaves a bottle of the old product behind somewhere upstream, and in this level it turns up as the third bottle of the next batch: a SODA bottle among the WATER, a WATER bottle among the JUICE. The camera has to catch it, and it does, because the job it is running knows what product it expects. And every bottle gets a trace record: the PLC tells the camera which bottle is coming (its position in the batch and its number on the line), the camera puts that into its answer, and the PLC files the answer in a STRING array. Twenty-four bottles, par 65 s.

The machine

The camera’s new tags

Everything from Level 8 still applies. These are the tags this level adds. They are the In-Sight 5700 series’ own names.

TagMeaning
Cam1:I.Current_Job_IDThe job the camera is running now (1, 2 or 3).
Cam1:O.Command_IDThe job to load when Execute_Command rises.
Cam1:O.Execute_CommandRising edge: run the command (here, load job Command_ID). Hold it until Command_Complete.
TagMeaning
Cam1:I.Command_CompleteThe command has finished; stays on until Execute_Command drops.
Cam1:I.Command_FailedThe command could not run, for example a job number the camera does not have.
Cam1:O.User_Data[…]Bytes the PLC sends with an inspection. The job reads bytes 0-1 as the bottle’s position in its batch and bytes 4-7 as its number on the line.
Cam1:O.Set_User_DataRising edge: the camera latches User_Data for the next trigger.
Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_AckThe camera has the data; stays on until Set_User_Data drops.
Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[12…
27]The trace: 16 ASCII characters, PRODUCT,PP,NNNNNN. PRODUCT is the job’s product, PP the position and NNNNNN the number the PLC sent.
Result code bit 4Wrong product: the bottle is not the product the running job expects. Any job, any bottle.

Three handshakes, in order

The job change. Put the job number in Command_ID and raise Execute_Command. The camera loads the job (about half a second, with Trigger_Ready off while it does), sets Current_Job_ID and raises Command_Complete. Drop Execute_Command and the camera drops Command_Complete. A trigger during the change is a missed acquisition. A bottle inspected under the wrong job gets the wrong verdict: a SODA bottle inspected under the WATER job is a wrong-product reject.

The user data. Before each trigger, write User_Data and raise Set_User_Data. Wait for Set_User_Data_Ack, then trigger. The camera ties the data it latched to the next image it takes. Trigger before the ack and the inspection carries the last bottle’s data.

The trigger and the result are Level 8’s, unchanged.

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
A defective or wrong-product bottle in Reject_Bin+100
A good bottle in Good_Bin+100
A defective bottle in Good_Bin (shipped)−100
A good bottle in Reject_Bin−50
A bottle that passes the camera without being inspected−25
Each Trace[n] that holds bottle n+1’s record exactly, checked at the end+25
Complete under par+200

The trace check compares Trace[0] to SODA,01,000001, Trace[1] to SODA,02,000002 and so on to Trace[23], JUICE,08,000024. The stray bottle’s record names the batch it was in, not the product it was: the 11th bottle is a SODA bottle in the WATER batch, and its record is WATER,03,000011. That is what the camera knows: the job it ran and the data it was sent.

How to pass it, step by step

1. Start from Level 8. Run, belt, camera setup, trigger, results FIFO, reject: all of it stays.

2. Work out the wanted job from the selector, every scan.

3. Gate the release on the job. A bottle leaves the hopper only while the camera is running the wanted

4. Wait for the line to clear once the hopper is held: 5 s is enough for the last bottle of the old batch to

5. Change the job, and drop Execute_Command on Command_Complete.

6. Send the user data with each trigger, and trigger only on the ack.

7. File the trace when each result is read.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

TagTypeKindDescription
Start_PBBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.10Start push button, momentary
RunBOOLbase tagSeal-in run bit
Stop_PBBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.11Stop push button, momentary
E_StopBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.12E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy
Conveyor_RunBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.1Belt motor
Lamp_RunBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.3Run lamp
Prod_SODABOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.8Product selector at SODA (left): the next batch is SODA
Want_JobDINTbase tagThe camera job the next batch needs: 1 SODA, 2 WATER, 3 JUICE
Prod_JUICEBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.9Product selector at JUICE (right); neither = WATER
Job_OKBOOLbase tagThe camera has that job loaded and no change is running
Infeed_ReadyBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.0Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released
Rel_TTIMERbase tagRelease interval
Infeed_ReleaseBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.0Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)
Clear_TTIMERbase tagLine clear: time for the last bottle of a batch to pass the camera
PE_TriggerBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.2Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view
Trig_ONSBOOLbase tag
Trig_ReqBOOLbase tag
Bottle_NoDINTbase tagBottles that have reached the camera, counted at the trigger eye
PosDINTbase tagThis bottle’s position in its batch, 1-8
Res_QDINTbase tagResult codes waiting for the reject eye
Res_Q_CtlCONTROLbase tag
Trace_IdxDINTbase tagNext free record in Trace
TraceSTRINGbase tagOne trace record per bottle, PRODUCT,PP,NNNNNN
PE_RejectBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.5Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher
Rej_ONSBOOLbase tag
CurDINTbase tagThe result code of the bottle at the reject eye
Rej_ONS2BOOLbase tag
FireBOOLbase tag
RejectBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.2Reject pusher cylinder
Cnt_ONSBOOLbase tag
Reject_CountDINTbase tagShown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected
Pass_CountDINTbase tagShown on the toolbar: bottles you let through
Lamp_FaultBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.4Fault lamp

Run, setup and the wanted job

Rung 3 is one rung with three legs, one per selector position. Exactly one leg is true at a time. With neither Prod_SODA nor Prod_JUICE on, the middle leg writes 2. Rung 4 is the gate for everything below it: Job_OK is on only when the camera’s job matches and no change is in progress. Because rung 3 is written before rung 4, the job is worked out and then tested in the same scan.

Release, only on the right job

Rung 5 is Level 8’s release timer with Job_OK in it. When the last SODA bottle leaves the hopper, the selector moves to WATER, Want_Job becomes 2, Job_OK drops and the timer stops: nothing more is released until the camera has job 2.

The changeover

Rung 7 counts the line-clear time from the moment the hopper is held. The last SODA bottle is somewhere between the hopper and the camera. At 80 px/s it needs about 4 s to reach the camera and pass it, and its result comes back 180 ms after that. Five seconds covers it. Rung 8 is the command: it fires once, because XIO(Cam1:O.Execute_Command) is in it and it latches Execute_Command. Rung 9 drops the command when the camera answers. On the next scan Current_Job_ID equals Want_Job and Execute_Command is off, so rung 4 sets Job_OK, rung 7 resets Clear_T and rung 5 starts releasing the WATER batch.

Watch for: changing job too soon

Take the 5 s out (Clear_T at 0) and the camera loads the WATER job while the last SODA bottle is still on its way. The last SODA bottles are inspected under WATER and rejected as the wrong product, −50 each for good bottles in Reject_Bin, and their trace records name the wrong batch. In the reference program with Clear_T at 0, six bottles go wrong and the score drops from 3200 to 2150. A bottle that reaches the camera during the half-second load is worse off still: its trigger is missed and it goes by with no image at all.

User data and the trigger

Rung 10 counts the bottle as it reaches the camera, so Bottle_No is its number on the line: 1 for the first SODA bottle, 24 for the last JUICE bottle. Rung 11 works out its position in the batch, ((Bottle_No-1) MOD 8)+1, and copies both numbers into User_Data. Pos is a DINT, so COP with a length of 4 copies its four bytes into User_Data[0] to [3]. Bottle_No goes into [4] to [7]. Rung 12 triggers only after the camera has acknowledged the data, and rung 13 drops both requests when the trigger is acknowledged. The next bottle gets fresh data.

The result and the trace

Rung 14 is Level 8’s result rung with one more branch. While Trace_Idx is under 24, COP copies the 16 trace bytes into Trace[Trace_Idx], then ADD moves the index on. The index addresses the array at run time, so one rung fills all 24 records in the order the results arrive, which is the order of the bottles. The LES stops it at the end of the array: Trace[24] does not exist, and writing to it would be a major fault.

The reject pusher, the counts and the fault lamp

These are Level 8’s, with one more fault on the lamp: Command_Failed. Ask for job 4, which this camera does not have, and the camera keeps job 1, raises Command_Failed instead of Command_Complete, and the line stays held. The lamp tells the operator why.

Run it

Load your program, Run mode, Start. Watch Product_Sel jump to WATER as the eighth SODA bottle leaves, the hopper hold, Camera_HMI’s JOB box change to Job 2: WATER (min fill 90 %), and the WATER batch start. The third WATER bottle has a red label: the camera fails it with code 16, WRONG, and the pusher takes it. In a run on v2.02, 24 of 24 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 54 s against a par of 65 s: 3200 points and three stars, and all 24 trace records right.

Try it: the wrong job

In rung 3, swap the 1 and the 3. The camera now runs JUICE on the SODA batch and SODA on the JUICE batch, and bit 4 fails every bottle in both, because none of them is the product the job expects. The reject bin fills with good bottles: 19 of the 24 end up there, and the score falls to about 1150. That is the changeover mistake a plant fears most, and the reason a camera job carries the product it expects.

Try it: trigger without the data

Take XIC(Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack) out of rung 12. Rungs 11 and 12 now go true in the same scan, so Set_User_Data and Trigger reach the camera in the same I/O update, and the camera takes the image before it has latched the data. Every record carries the previous bottle’s data: Trace[0] reads SODA,00,000000 and Trace[1] reads SODA,01,000001. The trace score falls to 0 while every bottle still lands in the right bin. A trace can be wrong while the product is right, so check the records as well as the bins.

Card mode on Level 9

Card mode works on Level 9 the same way it does on Level 8 (tick Card mode in the Camera’s properties): the hopper’s bottles wait at the camera and each takes the verdict of the card under the lens. What Level 9 adds is the product. A card is SN-48RK, R the product and K the defect, and the camera answers WRONG (bit 4) when the card’s product is not the loaded job’s. The bottle becomes what the card shows: under the SODA job a WATER card is a WATER bottle in the SODA batch, and it is rejected as a stray.

So the cards are swapped at the changeover, as an operator would swap product: when the camera loads WATER, put a WATER card under the lens. To give the camera its stray, show it the old product’s card for a bottle or two after the change; the level’s stray check is met when one of those is rejected. The CARDS page opens on the loaded job’s product, marks it on its tab (JOB: at the top right) and lists what each card of the row should read under that job.

With the camera live, the real job decides. The page reads the card from byte 10 (R × 10 + K) and the loaded job from Current_Job_ID, and counts a result right when the code matches the card’s defect plus WRONG for a card of another product. Your In-Sight job does the same: decode the DataMatrix for R and K, read the label with OCR, and set bit 4 when the text is not the job’s product.

Try it: run level 9 on cards

Tick Card mode with SN-4801 under the lens and run your Level 9 program. When Product_Sel turns to WATER and the camera loads job 2, leave SN-4801 there for two more bottles: both read WRONG and go to the reject bin. Then touch the WATER tab and SN-4811, and at the JUICE change SN-4831. The level completes, and the score card lists SN-4801 with its WRONG reads counted as right.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt runs with the line; it never stops for the camera
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: CAMERA SETUP: triggering enabled and results buffered, as in Level 8

pred.q: E_Stop is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable is off and Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable is off. It stops at XIC(E_Stop).

rungs.words: When E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: WANTED JOB: one leg per selector position. The selector shows the batch the next bottle belongs to
rungs.words: Each path is tested on its own: if Prod_SODA (Product selector at SODA (left): the next batch is SODA) is on, it puts 1 into Want_Job (The camera job the next batch needs: 1 SODA, 2 WATER, 3 JUICE); if Prod_SODA is off and Prod_JUICE (Product selector at JUICE (right); neither = WATER) is off, it puts 2 into Want_Job; if Prod_JUICE is on, it puts 3 into Want_Job.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Prod_SODA) Examine If Closed asks: true when Prod_SODA is on.
    2. MOV(1,Want_Job) Move does: puts 1 into Want_Job. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Prod_SODA) Examine If Open asks: true when Prod_SODA is off.
    2. XIO(Prod_JUICE) Examine If Open asks: true when Prod_JUICE is off.
    3. MOV(2,Want_Job) Move does: puts 2 into Want_Job. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Prod_JUICE) Examine If Closed asks: true when Prod_JUICE is on.
    2. MOV(3,Want_Job) Move does: puts 3 into Want_Job. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: JOB OK: the camera is running the job the next batch needs, and no change is in progress
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Current_Job_ID equals Want_Job (The camera job the next batch needs: 1 SODA, 2 WATER, 3 JUICE) and Cam1:O.Execute_Command is off, the rung turns Job_OK (The camera has that job loaded and no change is running) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Cam1:I.Current_Job_ID,Want_Job) Equal asks: true when Cam1:I.Current_Job_ID equals Want_Job. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Execute_Command) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Execute_Command is off.
  3. OTE(Job_OK) Output Energize does: turns Job_OK on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: RELEASE a bottle every 0.9 s, but only while the camera has the right job: at a new batch the hopper is held
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Job_OK (The camera has that job loaded and no change is running) is on, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Release interval) is off, the rung runs the timer Rel_T (Release interval) toward 900 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Job_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Job_OK is on.
  3. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  4. XIO(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when Rel_T.DN is off.
  5. TON(Rel_T,900,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Rel_T toward 900 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Rel_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 6

pred.q: Rel_T.DN is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Infeed_Release is on.

rungs.words: When Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Release interval) is on, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rel_T.DN is on.
  2. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: LINE CLEAR: the hopper is held; give the last bottle of the old batch 5 s to pass the camera before its job changes (hopper to camera is about 4 s)
rungs.words: When Job_OK (The camera has that job loaded and no change is running) is off, the rung runs the timer Clear_T (Line clear: time for the last bottle of a batch to pass the camera) toward 5000 ms (5 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Job_OK) Examine If Open asks: true when Job_OK is off.
  2. TON(Clear_T,5000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Clear_T toward 5000 ms (5 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Clear_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: CHANGE THE JOB: the job number in Command_ID, then Execute_Command

pred.q: Clear_T.DN is off, Cam1:O.Execute_Command is on and Cam1:I.Command_Complete is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Command_ID is not written (it keeps its value) and Cam1:O.Execute_Command is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Clear_T.DN).

rungs.words: When Clear_T.DN (the done bit of Clear_T: Line clear: time for the last bottle of a batch to pass the camera) is on, Cam1:O.Execute_Command is off and Cam1:I.Command_Complete is off, the rung puts Want_Job (The camera job the next batch needs: 1 SODA, 2 WATER, 3 JUICE) into Cam1:O.Command_ID and latches Cam1:O.Execute_Command on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Clear_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Clear_T.DN is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Execute_Command) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Execute_Command is off.
  3. XIO(Cam1:I.Command_Complete) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Command_Complete is off.
  4. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Want_Job,Cam1:O.Command_ID) Move does: puts Want_Job into Cam1:O.Command_ID. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Execute_Command) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Execute_Command on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Execute_Command stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: The camera has loaded it: drop Execute_Command. Current_Job_ID now matches, Job_OK comes on and the hopper releases the new batch
rungs.words: When Cam1:O.Execute_Command is on and Cam1:I.Command_Complete is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Execute_Command.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:O.Execute_Command) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:O.Execute_Command is on.
  2. XIC(Cam1:I.Command_Complete) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Command_Complete is on.
  3. OTU(Cam1:O.Execute_Command) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Execute_Command. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Execute_Command when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: A BOTTLE AT THE CAMERA: ask for a trigger and count it
rungs.words: When PE_Trigger (Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Trig_Req on and makes Bottle_No (Bottles that have reached the camera, counted at the trigger eye) = Bottle_No + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Trigger is on.
  2. ONS(Trig_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Trig_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Trig_Req) Output Latch does: latches Trig_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. ADD(Bottle_No,1,Bottle_No) Add does: makes Bottle_No = Bottle_No + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.why: Trig_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: USER DATA first: this bottle’s position in its batch (bytes 0-3) and its number (bytes 4-7), then Set_User_Data
rungs.words: When Trig_Req is on and Cam1:O.Set_User_Data is off, the rung computes Pos (This bottle’s position in its batch, 1-8) = ((Bottle_No-1) MOD 8)+1, copies 4 elements from Pos to Cam1:O.User_Data[0], copies 4 elements from Bottle_No (Bottles that have reached the camera, counted at the trigger eye) to Cam1:O.User_Data[4] and latches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Set_User_Data) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Set_User_Data is off.
  3. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. CPT(Pos,((Bottle_No-1) MOD 8)+1) Compute does: computes Pos = ((Bottle_No-1) MOD 8)+1.
    Path 2
    1. COP(Pos,Cam1:O.User_Data[0],4) Copy File does: copies 4 elements from Pos to Cam1:O.User_Data[0].
    Path 3
    1. COP(Bottle_No,Cam1:O.User_Data[4],4) Copy File does: copies 4 elements from Bottle_No to Cam1:O.User_Data[4].
    Path 4
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Set_User_Data) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Set_User_Data stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: TRIGGER once the camera has taken the data and is ready

pred.q: Trig_Req is on, Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cam1:O.Trigger latches on.

rungs.words: When Trig_Req is on, Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIC(Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Set_User_Data_Ack is on.
  3. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  4. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: Acknowledged: drop the trigger and the data request
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger, unlatches Trig_Req and unlatches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Trig_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Trig_Req. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Set_User_Data) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Set_User_Data. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: RESULT: the code into the FIFO for the reject, the trace string (bytes 12-27) into the next Trace record, then acknowledge
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, each path is tested on its own: it loads Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into the queue Res_Q[0] (Result codes waiting for the reject eye); if Trace_Idx (Next free record in Trace) is less than 24, it copies 16 elements from Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[12] to Trace[Trace_Idx] (One trace record per bottle, PRODUCT,PP,NNNNNN) and makes Trace_Idx = Trace_Idx + 1; it latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFL(Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code,Res_Q[0],Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into the queue Res_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. LES(Trace_Idx,24) Less Than asks: true when Trace_Idx is less than 24.
    2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
      Path 1
      1. COP(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[12],Trace[Trace_Idx],16) Copy File does: copies 16 elements from Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[12] to Trace[Trace_Idx].
      Path 2
      1. ADD(Trace_Idx,1,Trace_Idx) Add does: makes Trace_Idx = Trace_Idx + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 3
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: Valid has gone: drop the ack, ready for the next result
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: REJECT: a bottle at the reject eye takes the oldest result
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] (Result codes waiting for the reject eye) into Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject eye).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFU(Res_Q[0],Cur,Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] into Cur. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: Any bit set, the wrong product included: arm the pusher
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on, this is the first scan of it and Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject eye) is not 0, the rung latches Fire on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS2) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS2). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. NEQ(Cur,0) Not Equal asks: true when Cur is not 0.
  4. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fire stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: Push while the bottle is at the eye

pred.q: PE_Reject is off and Fire is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Reject is off. It stops at XIC(PE_Reject).

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and Fire is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  3. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: COUNTS on the toolbar
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if Fire is on, it makes Reject_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected) = Reject_Count + 1; if Fire is off, it makes Pass_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through) = Pass_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Cnt_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cnt_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
    2. ADD(Reject_Count,1,Reject_Count) Add does: makes Reject_Count = Reject_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Fire) Examine If Open asks: true when Fire is off.
    2. ADD(Pass_Count,1,Pass_Count) Add does: makes Pass_Count = Pass_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: The bottle has gone: disarm

pred.q: PE_Reject is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Fire is unlatched.

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is off, the rung unlatches Fire.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  2. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: FAULT LAMP: a lost result, a missed acquisition, the camera offline or a job change that failed
rungs.words: When either (Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on), (Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on), (Cam1:I.Online is off) or (Cam1:I.Command_Failed is on), the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 4 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Missed_Acq) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(Cam1:I.Online) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Online is off.
    Path 4
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Command_Failed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Command_Failed is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Prod_SODA.desc: Product selector at SODA (left): the next batch is SODA

Want_Job.desc: The camera job the next batch needs: 1 SODA, 2 WATER, 3 JUICE

Prod_JUICE.desc: Product selector at JUICE (right); neither = WATER

Job_OK.desc: The camera has that job loaded and no change is running

Infeed_Ready.desc: Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released

Infeed_Release.desc: Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)

Clear_T.desc: Line clear: time for the last bottle of a batch to pass the camera

PE_Trigger.desc: Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view

Bottle_No.desc: Bottles that have reached the camera, counted at the trigger eye

Pos.desc: This bottle’s position in its batch, 1-8

Res_Q.desc: Result codes waiting for the reject eye

Trace.desc: One trace record per bottle, PRODUCT,PP,NNNNNN

PE_Reject.desc: Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher

Cur.desc: The result code of the bottle at the reject eye

Reject_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected

Pass_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through
